text:
alex: heads up — saw a 15-40ms tail at host ingress after yesterday's batching tweak.
mira: which path? http/gRPC or proxy? :eyes:
alex: host proxy -> tokenizer handoff. traces show stalled writev coalescing on ~2% of requests.
jon: interesting, any relation to the new chunk scheduler heuristic? we changed target window from 12ms -> 8ms.
alex: yeah timeline matches the rollout. reduced window means more small frames; gRPC hpack overhead spikes.
kim: can you paste the perf sample? small snippet of pprof or traces is fine.
alex: here — grabbed a flame snippet from the repro run:
```
12:34:10.123 host_proxy.writev 8.2ms
12:34:10.131 tokenizer.queue_wait 9.7ms
12:34:10.141 grpc.hpack_encode 4.1ms
12:34:10.145 kernel.writev syscall 7.8ms
```
mira: hmm kernel syscalls dominating. Are we doing synchronous writes for small chunks? should we batch earlier in user-space?
jon: the scheduler change aimed to reduce latency by flushing faster; but if tokenizer still emits many tiny fragments, syscall overhead kills us.
kim: what about combining prefix tokens on host before writev? i.e. merge consecutive tokenized buffers up to 16KB before syscall.
alex: tried that in a quick patch — lowered median by 6ms on local but tail still high for high QPS flows.
sre-bot: incident-created #ingress-chunk-surge — severity: low, owner: eng-runtime
mira: can you reproduce with KV cache warm vs cold? maybe KV cache evictions add jitter to tokenizer timing.
alex: good call — warm cache run reduces queue_wait variance. with cold cache, tokenizer spikes align with kvcache misses.
jon: plausible — kvcache miss triggers more model-side CPU blocking which changes scheduling; combined with smaller host flush windows -> more small writes.
kim: options:
- increase scheduler window for host-proxy to 12-16ms (roll back tweak)
- do a tokenizer-side coalescer before writev
- heuristically fuse writes when kvcache miss latency > X
alex: also saw kernel-level wakeups clustered — maybe wakeup->write syscall ordering causing contention. could try user-space coalescing + async writev.
mira: can we quickly A/B rollback window in canary? deploy-bot, can we schedule a 10% canary to revert window to 12ms?
deploy-bot: scheduling canary: eng-runtime/canary-10pct rollback-window=12ms — started 3980012355
jon: while canary runs, alex/kim, please prototype tokenizer coalescer and measure syscall count per request.
alex: on it. I'll instrument count and push a tiny knob.
kim: i'll add a probe to trace when kvcache miss happens to correlate with syscall spikes.
sre-bot: canary halfway through — no regression detected in overall P99 error rate yet, but host ingress P95 down ~4ms for canary nodes.
mira: good. if canary looks promising we should do gradual rollback and follow with tokenizer coalescer as a follow-up.
alex: FYI patch notes I'll try:
```
- host/proxy: backlog_window_ms = 12 (canary)
- tokenizer: add coalesce_writebufs(up_to=16KB, max_items=8)
- trace: emit kvcache_miss tag for ingress spans
```
jon: sounds good. also add metric: writev_syscalls_per_request.
kim: agreed. will add kvcache_miss rate and correlate in console dashboard.
alex: logging quick perf from local patch: syscalls/request dropped from 3.1 -> 1.2 and median ingress down 5.9ms.
mira: awesome — let's let canary finish and reconvene. thanks all :thumbsup:
alex: filing follow-up PR and will paste link when ready.
jon: thanks, team. keep the thread updated.
